guidance.procedure: For each hypothesis independently align actor, modality, action, object, quantifier, trigger, conditions and exceptions before selecting evidence. Silence and neighboring topics are unresolved; never infer permission from absence, a trigger from survival, or one relationship from another. Select every original member independently expressing the governing rule, responsive repetition, necessary scope or operative exception. Headings, recitals and consequences are not members merely by proximity, but retain them when they actually supply a governing object, purpose, condition or responsive proposition.

Decide endpoint disposition and post-disposition retention independently. For disposition, “upon request, return or destroy” alone is unresolved for termination; an operative termination, expiration, completed-evaluation, abandoned-dealings or ended-need trigger supports when it governs the remedy. Either return or destruction of any covered subset suffices. For retention, inspect the same sentence for exceptions: “retain one secured or legal copy,” “law-required records,” or “automated backups need not be erased” supports possession; cite the disposition introduction and every independently retained category. Conversely, “return all originals and copies without retaining reproductions,” “certify every copy destroyed,” or return/destruction plus “retain in no form whatsoever” opposes retention; cite every component establishing completeness. A bare return duty neither permits nor opposes retention, and an endpoint disposition rule must never be relabeled as retention permission.

Identify both the duty and the endpoint it can outlast. Express continuation after termination, expiration, completed dealings or return supports. So does a confidentiality duration that can extend beyond an independently available termination point, an indefinite protected-duty period, retained material remaining subject to duties, or a statement that disposition does not discharge duties. Pattern: “either party may terminate at any time; confidentiality continues for five years” supports; “the agreement lasts five years” alone does not. A request-only return duty, later possible end date, remedy for an earlier breach or exception without a continuing duty is insufficient. Cite every separately responsive continuation or duration provision and short connector needed to identify what continues, but not an ordinary term clause merely because it states a date.

Locate the operative definition or incorporated coverage before classifying subject matter. Technical-only is supported only when every coverage route is confined to technical, engineering, software or comparable system material. It is opposed by an expressly covered business, financial, commercial, operational, personnel, lease, marketing, customer or similar nontechnical category; a broad operative combination such as non-public information, know-how and trade secrets can also defeat exclusivity. Bare “information,” “data,” “any form,” oral/written media, marking language, or technical/commercial words in a clause saying disclosure is unnecessary are unresolved. Pattern: “technical specifications and source code” may support; “technical specifications, pricing and customer plans” opposes; “information furnished for discussions, orally or in writing” alone does neither. Cite only the definition lead, incorporated premise and decisive categories, never the surrounding agreement wholesale.

Resolve the two source routes independently. Independent development needs an express exclusion or allowance for creation, development, discovery or acquisition by the recipient or its personnel without using or accessing protected information. A separate affirmative statement that similar or competing products may be developed also supports. Prior possession, public availability, third-party receipt, silence and generic competitive activity do not substitute. Third-party acquisition needs an express lawful, authorized, unrestricted or nonconfidential third-party source route, preserving knowledge, authorization and no-duty conditions; recipient development does not substitute. Pattern: “previously possessed or received from an unrestricted source” supports only the stated routes, not independent development. Cite the operative exclusion introduction, qualifying branch, and every separately operative similar-information permission; omit unrelated exclusion branches.

Evaluate employee and nonemployee sharing separately from the operative permission or ban. “May disclose to representatives,” with representatives defined to include employees and advisers, supports both classes; cite the permission, needed definition and operative conditions. “Disclose within the recipient only on a need-to-know basis” supports employee access but opposes outside third-party sharing. Likewise, “do not disclose to third parties or employees except employees who need it,” or an employee-access clause paired with a third-party ban, supports employees and opposes third parties. Employee access alone is unresolved for third parties unless exclusivity or a ban reaches outsiders. A definition, countersignature, responsibility or protection clause is not permission, though language expressly recognizing that named persons may receive or access can complete an elliptical authorization. A fresh-consent-only route opposes the covered class. Select every operative recipient branch and condition, but exclude pure breach and liability provisions.

Support no-license from an express no-rights or no-license rule, retained or exclusive ownership, or a property reservation covering the protected information or associated intellectual-property rights. Pattern: “the information remains the owner’s property and no license is granted” supports; “no rights are acquired except limited use for the project” also supports because the purpose-use privilege is not a proprietary grant. A warranty disclaimer, no-commitment clause, permission to evaluate, or silence does not establish no-license. A license concerning separate marks, products or services is nonresponsive. Oppose only when an affirmative license actually reaches the protected information or its associated rights. Cite each independently operative ownership, rights-reservation and no-license provision, including bilateral counterparts.

Inspect confidentiality, announcements, publicity and communications provisions for a duty covering agreement-related facts: existence of the agreement or relationship, fact of exchanged access, transaction communications, discussions or negotiations, status, terms, conditions or arrangement. Pattern: “communications between the parties concerning the contemplated transaction are confidential” supports when an operative nondisclosure duty governs those communications; “information furnished about the business is confidential” alone does not. A rule forbidding disclosure that the subject of an exchange is known to the parties can support the fact of the confidential exchange, but a ban on associating oneself with a customer or using a name alone is unresolved. Cite the operative duty and each separately responsive listed fact, plus a definition only when it supplies that fact.

Require an operative restriction on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing, approaching or offering participation to a protected person. Employee patterns cover the discloser’s employees, officers, agents or consultants, subject to duration and general-advertisement exceptions. A broad prohibition on directly contacting the other party’s clients for any reason without consent can also be responsive; distinguish it from a mere noncircumvention or negotiation rule concerning business contacts. Likewise, forbidding an offer to outsiders of equity or joint participation in the contemplated transaction can support, while a clause merely regulating whether the transaction closes does not. Customer, supplier, business-source and named-contact provisions otherwise remain unresolved unless their operative act is the annotated solicitation or broad contact ban. Cite the restriction and responsive target branch, excluding adjacent standstill and communication mechanics.

Copy permission requires an affirmative allowance or an exception that itself authorizes making copies in stated circumstances. Pattern: “a limited number of copies may be made for evaluation” supports. A command not to copy, reproduce, duplicate or make copies opposes permission, including consent-qualified bans and a discloser’s operative notice that identified material is not to be reproduced. Cite the governing introduction or notice and the actual copying command. Existing copies, return or destruction duties, no-retention language, proprietary notices placed on copies, backups and references to documents do not authorize creation and are not substitutes for the copying provision. A negative clause containing “unless” supports only if its exception affirmatively grants copying authority.

Require an affirmative notice duty tied to disclosure compelled by law, regulation, subpoena, judicial process or governmental demand. The duty may appear inside a permitted-disclosure clause or an exclusion: “law-required disclosure, provided advance notice is given” supports and requires the governing trigger plus notice branch. Counterpattern: “information may be disclosed as required by law” alone authorizes disclosure but supplies no notice duty; never infer notice from permission, cooperation or protective-treatment language. Notice of an unauthorized breach is also nonresponsive. Preserve legal-permission, practicability and timing qualifications. When separate governmental-demand or public-records branches each impose notice, cite each complete trigger-and-notice route; omit later minimum-disclosure steps unless they qualify notice.

Support limited use only when an operative rule makes the agreement’s evaluation, transaction, project, business-relationship or performance purpose exclusive. Pattern: “use only to evaluate the transaction” supports; “do not use the information in an independent business” is unresolved because it bans one use without making the stated contractual purpose exclusive. A total use ban with no permitted contractual purpose is likewise unresolved, not opposition. Match actor and protected object: nondisclosure, employee access, return, ownership, assignment and copying do not substitute. Scan for separate protected categories and repetitions, including an introductory exclusivity rule and later no-use continuation, and cite every independently operative exclusive-purpose restriction plus only the clause needed to supply its purpose.

Ask whether every route into protection requires the discloser to mark, designate, identify or give a qualifying notice. Pattern: “protected information means material marked confidential” supports when no alternative route exists. “Marked confidential or reasonably understood from its character or circumstances to be confidential” opposes because the objective route needs no identifying act. Broad phrases such as “all information disclosed by the owner,” “all information received,” or “information disclosed during the event” are unresolved: source or automatic receipt is not identification, but does not itself establish an express no-identification route. A later written summary of oral material proves universality only if that identification condition governs every route. Cite the definition lead and all alternative qualification routes necessary to test universality; omit subject-matter examples and exclusions.

Require an operative route covering information received orally, verbally, visually, by hearing, in nonwritten form, or whether or not reduced to tangible form; a required later written confirmation can condition but still support that route. Generic “in any form,” “technical data,” “know-how,” or an oral method of the recipient’s prohibited disclosure does not establish that orally received information is protected. Pattern: “oral or written disclosures are confidential” supports; “confidential information in any form” alone is unresolved; “do not reveal it verbally or in writing” regulates the recipient’s act and does not support oral coverage. Cite the definition or confirmation route and any independently operative continuation specifically governing oral material, not adjacent subject matter, marking or use clauses.

Require reverse engineering by name or a functionally specified extraction act applied to the protected object. Pattern: a governing undertaking followed by “do not analyze a sample to determine its chemical structure or composition” supports; cite both the short undertaking supplying actor or modality and the extraction command. Decompiling, disassembling, decoding or extracting design or composition likewise supports. A definition merely identifying confidential material is not evidence of the prohibition, even if another clause later says “disassemble.” Testing authorization, ordinary copying restrictions, purpose-use limits, development limits and generic nondisclosure do not substitute unless they expressly prohibit extracting structure or design. Cite every responsive extraction prohibition, excluding adjacent sample-security and evaluation provisions.

Decide endpoint disposition and retention separately. For disposition, the remedy must be governed by termination, expiration, abandoned dealings, completed evaluation or ended need. Pattern: “upon termination, return or destroy the files” supports; “upon request, return or destroy the files” and “materials will be confidentially disposed of” are unresolved because neither supplies the endpoint. Do not turn disposal without that trigger into opposition. For retention, an express retained legal, archival or backup copy supports, while return or destruction of all originals and copies, no retained reproductions, or deletion from storage opposes. A bare return duty is unresolved. Cite the trigger and remedy; for a retention exception, include the disposition clause only when it supplies necessary scope or the antecedent, not automatically.

operations.rationale: The lawyer repeatedly converted request-only or untriggered disposition into termination disposition, while also confusing comprehensive copy removal, retention exceptions and the evidence needed to connect them.

guidance.procedure: Identify a duty and an endpoint it outlasts. Express continuation after termination, expiration, ended dealings or return supports; so does a duty period extending beyond a separately stated earlier termination point, or an indefinite operative duty recognized by the agreement. Pattern: “either party may terminate now; confidentiality continues three years” supports. Conversely, “all obligations expire after five years” or “upon termination neither party has further obligations” opposes survival unless another provision preserves a duty. A term, solicitation period, possible closing date, request-only return duty, remedy or breach consequence does not support merely because it has a duration. Cite each independently responsive continuation or cessation provision and only the endpoint connector needed to compare durations.

operations.rationale: The existing duration language encouraged express expiration of all duties and shorter standalone restrictions to be read as survival, while an indefinite operative term was missed.

guidance.procedure: Evaluate employee and nonemployee recipients independently. “May disclose to representatives,” with representatives including employees and advisers, supports both; cite the permission, necessary definition and operative conditions. A negative formulation may also authorize an exception: “do not disclose to anyone, including employees, who lacks a need to know” supports access by the stated need-to-know class. Counterpattern: “do not disclose to third parties or employees except need-to-know employees” supports employees but opposes outside third parties. “Disclose only within the recipient” likewise supports employees and opposes outsiders. A standalone statement that employees already have access, must sign, are informed, or create recipient liability is not permission. Fresh-consent-only disclosure opposes the covered class. Select each responsive recipient branch, but omit pure protection, breach and responsibility terms.

operations.rationale: The lawyer continued swapping employee and outsider classes, treating standalone access acknowledgments as permission, and overlooking permissions expressed as exceptions to negative need-to-know clauses.

guidance.procedure: Resolve the source routes separately. Independent development requires creation, development or discovery by the recipient without using or accessing protected information, or an affirmative similar-product development permission. Third-party acquisition requires lawful, authorized, unrestricted or nonconfidential receipt, or an express right to acquire products or receive similar information from others. Pattern: “may independently develop competing products” supports development only; “may acquire products or receive similar information from others” supports third-party acquisition; a clause containing both supports its stated routes. Prior possession, public availability and silence do not substitute. Restrictions on disclosure, copying, business use or employee access neither oppose nor establish either route. Cite the operative exclusion lead when it governs the branch and every separately operative similar-information permission, without borrowing a development-only branch for third-party acquisition.

operations.rationale: The lawyer inferred opposition from unrelated restrictions and alternated between collapsing development into third-party acquisition and missing express acquisition or similar-information routes.

guidance.procedure: Classify only authority to make a new copy. “May reproduce or make limited copies solely for evaluation” supports. “Do not copy, reproduce or duplicate,” including a consent-gated ban or an operative notice that identified material is not to be reproduced, opposes. Pattern: “return all existing copies without retaining reproductions” addresses disposition and is unresolved for whether copies could originally be made; “copies may be made for the project” directly supports. Existing copies, archival retention, backups, proprietary legends, document references, general use permission and nondisclosure do not establish copying authority. Cite the actual copying permission or command and any short governing introduction or notice supplying its actor or object; never replace it with a definition, return clause or neighboring use restriction.

operations.rationale: The prior rule was still ignored: the lawyer derived copying verdicts from use and return provisions, missed an express reproduction permission, and missed the actual notice-based no-reproduction command.

Coverage may be direct or arise because the definition makes those facts Confidential Information and the nondisclosure duty governs that definition. Select the definition lead and each responsive agreement-fact branch; add the nondisclosure provision when it independently supplies the governing duty, but omit unrelated transaction, publicity and remedy clauses.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed agreement-existence coverage embedded in a Confidential Information definition and repeatedly omitted the definition lead or responsive negotiation branches.

guidance.procedure: Support limited use when an operative rule makes the stated evaluation, transaction, project, relationship or performance purpose exclusive. This includes a narrower act involving the protected information when that act is expressly allowed only for the contractual purpose, such as “Confidential Information may be reproduced solely for evaluation.” A ban on one unrelated use or a total use ban with no permitted contractual purpose is unresolved. An affirmative exception allowing protected residual information to be used “for any purpose” opposes exclusivity for that covered category, even if confidentiality remains required. Match actor and object: nondisclosure, employee access, return, ownership and assignment do not substitute. Cite every independently operative exclusive-purpose rule or contrary any-purpose exception, plus only the clause needed to supply its purpose or protected object.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed purpose-limited reproduction and repeated restrictions, while treating an affirmative any-purpose residuals exception as supporting rather than opposing exclusive contractual-purpose use.
